input.title: Data in · df
input.cmd: uv run --quiet --with pandas python examples/trace-dropna.py df

steps.title: .dropna(): remove any row that has a blank
steps.plain: Row 09:01 has a blank in sensor B, so the whole row goes, including sensor A's valid 12.0.
steps.cmd: uv run --quiet --with pandas python examples/trace-dropna.py dropna

steps.title: .mean(): average each column
steps.plain: Sensor A is (10 + 18) / 2. Sensor B is (20 + 26) / 2.
steps.cmd: uv run --quiet --with pandas python examples/trace-dropna.py mean

summary: 3 rows go in, 2 survive, 2 averages come out. Without .dropna(), df.mean() would give sensor A 13.33, because the 12.0 would be kept.
